invariant: A composite containing an entry or exit border point is non-autarkic and remains a live cluster in the root Graphviz graph, including when sibling-group links use named left/up directions or reverse-arrow syntax. Transition command orientation and link inversion are independent: the reverse command initially exchanges textual endpoint roles; LEFT/UP then calls Link.getInv, which exchanges the stored endpoints and moves the arrow decoration to the path start. Thus a default `<--` link retains textual endpoint order in the solved graph but uses horizontal rank length zero and a start arrow, while a forward `-left->` link reverses solved endpoints and also uses a start arrow. For the basic port branch selected when each border label's integer width is at most 40px, input points occupy the cluster's source rank, outputs occupy its sink rank, both use 12-by-12 RECTANGLE_PORT nodes, entry-point links bypass ordinary rank-same handling, and the visible cluster frontier is derived from normal interior boxes plus the border-point centers. Java lays out and paints root composites in group-declaration order even when transitions referenced those names earlier; every leaf of one root composite precedes every leaf of the next, and unpackaged root leaves follow the grouped leaves. During edge solving, each link adjusts only the last declaration-ordered border cluster among its stored group endpoints before compound clipping; all border clusters are adjusted later for painting. DotPath compound clipping uses RectangleArea's half-open containment predicate: minimum edges are inside and maximum edges are outside.
causal_divergence: Java Entity.isAutarkic explicitly rejects groups containing non-normal leaves, so CucaDiagramSimplifierState leaves an entry/exit composite in the root GraphvizImageBuilder. CommandLinkStateReverse parses the textual left endpoint as ENT2 and the right endpoint as ENT1 and supplies default LEFT; CommandLinkStateCommon builds that logical link, then Link.getInv independently reverses stored endpoints and decorations for LEFT/UP. Rust's generic transition parser preserves only textual endpoint order, while its renderer reconstructs named direction tokens and conflates stored-endpoint reversal with start-arrow decoration. It also excludes LEFT/UP transitions from render_non_autarkic_root_clusters entirely. ClusterDotString constructs source and sink ranks and, during declaration-ordered group traversal, repeatedly assigns projectionCluster to links touching each group, so the later endpoint wins. DotStringFactory.solve visits links in insertion order; SvekEdge.solveLine adjusts only that selected projection cluster immediately before DotPath.simulateCompound. Rust's compound predicate additionally included the maximum rectangle edges, unlike Java RectangleArea.contains, so boundary-equal subdivided cubics survived or disappeared at different iterations. Cluster.drawU adjusts every border frontier later. GraphvizImageBuilder.printGroups and printGroup also create each group's leaves together in Bibliotekon's LinkedHashMap, and SvekResult.drawU paints that order after all cluster chrome.
planned_change: Make command orientation and effective direction first-class transition data in the parser instead of recovering them ad hoc from source text. Derive solved endpoint order as command-reversed XOR LEFT/UP inversion, derive start-arrow decoration from LEFT/UP inversion alone, and derive horizontal rank/minlen from LEFT/RIGHT. Use those independent properties consistently for Graphviz node/edge ordering, link IDs/comments/data endpoints, path selection, arrow retraction, and projection-cluster selection. Admit named LEFT/UP and reverse-arrow links to render_non_autarkic_root_clusters. Make compound clipping use Java RectangleArea's half-open maximum edges during all eight subdivision steps. Preserve declaration-ordered groups, basic 12-by-12 port nodes, source/sink ranks, stateful per-link frontier promotion, and adjusted final painting. The wider-label plaintext HTML-port branch is a separate mechanism because the vendored Graphviz build has no Expat table parser.
